title: Adidas Tokyo
meta_description: Adidas Tokyo is a neo-noir concept film told from the victim's point of view, where the sneaker is withheld until it is the last image left on screen.
deck: A neo-noir concept film told from the point of view of the person being walked toward. A hired assassin called Tokyo arrives, the tension builds, the shot is fired — and the last thing the victim sees is the sneaker “Tokyo”.

proof.title: The last shoe you’ll see.
proof.note: A shoe campaign normally opens on the shoe. Here the sneaker is written into the brief as critical and not to be revealed explicitly until the final scene, so every beat before it is spent building the tension the product has to occupy. The most memorable frame in the film is the one it spends the whole film refusing to show.

shots.alt: Night street seen from behind a figure in a navy adidas jacket, the trefoil across the back, facing a lit corner building with parked cars.
shots.caption: Stripe 1 / the approach

shots.alt: The same figure turning back toward the camera on the same street, a plaster on one cheek, the three stripes running down the sleeve.
shots.caption: Stripe 3 / the turn

proof.caption: Neo-noir shot as surveillance: high contrast, subtle desaturation, clean composition, and the camera moved only where the movement is meant to be felt. Park Chan-wook's atmosphere and Fincher's precision, with Tarantino's cult of footwear held back for the last frame.

acts.title: Build-up, then payoff.
acts.note: Nine boarded beats on one rising line, every one of them shot through a lens or from below, so the audience never gets to be the one doing the approaching.

items.title: The elevator
items.copy: CCTV, top-down, cold. Tokyo stands still, then looks up into the lens: “My name is Tokyo.”

items.title: The door
items.copy: A corridor at a Dutch angle, a doorbell pressed into a fisheye lens, the signal tearing. “You ask why?”

items.title: The floor
items.copy: Fragments — steps, aiming, the fall. “Because…”, delivered with pauses. Then ground level, a figure standing over, and the shoe.

pipeline.title: Pipeline.
pipeline.note: The character was locked before the film was, because a generative shoot drifts. A face, a tracksuit, and a sneaker all had to survive nine scenes without quietly redesigning themselves.

items.label: Reference
items.copy: Pinterest crossed with Midjourney portraits until one face held: fine features, uneven shoulder-length hair, a bandage on the cheek.

items.label: Contract
items.copy: The result written down as keywords and marked critical — the guarded eyes, the navy tracksuit, the sneaker's exact proportions. None of them free to change.

items.label: Generate
items.copy: A character sheet built first, then every scene and product frame generated from it, with Higgsfield carrying the motion.

items.label: Release
items.copy: Cut vertical and posted as numbered stripes rather than one film, so the payoff arrives on its own.
